 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Dale Earnhardt Jr. spent two decades building one of the most recognizable careers in NASCAR history . He won 26 Cup Series races, earned 15 consecutive Most Popular Driver awards and became one of the sport's biggest stars.
 There's just one problem.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement His own daughters don't seem to believe he ever raced.
 Earnhardt and his wife, Amy, shared the hilarious revelation during a recent episode of their "Bless Your 'Hardt" podcast , recorded live in Key West, Florida.
 And judging by their conversation, the two-time Daytona 500 winner has some convincing to do.
 Dale Earnhardt Jr.'s Daughters Aren't Buying His NASCAR Career
 The conversation began with Earnhardt reflecting on how much his daughters, Isla and Nicole, have been able to experience around NASCAR.
 Amy, however, pointed out that the girls might not fully appreciate their father's place in the sport.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I still don't think they get it," she said.
 Earnhardt agreed, admitting he's struggled to convince his daughters that the driver they see in old racing footage is actually their dad.
 "I can't convince Isla and Nicole that I'm in the race car," Earnhardt said. "Like when I show them videos."
 Amy recalled an equally amusing exchange during a recent race weekend.
 "When we were in the suite, they asked me if you were racing," she explained. "I'm like, you saw him beforehand. He didn't even have a helmet on."
 For a driver whose career included some of NASCAR's most memorable moments, the disconnect is almost impossible not to laugh at.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Amy Earnhardt Has the Perfect Response
 Earnhardt admitted he'd always assumed his daughters would eventually understand just how big a part of his life racing had been.
 "I felt like I was at some point going to be able to convince them of this," he said, reflecting on his Budweiser-sponsored years and the height of his popularity in 2004.
 "They're never going to get it. They're never going to know."
 Amy then delivered perhaps the funniest line of the entire conversation.
 "He's just the guy that drives everybody to school."
 Earnhardt couldn't argue with that.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I know, that's probably good," he replied.
 It's a pretty remarkable contrast for someone who spent much of his adult life racing in front of packed grandstands and millions of television viewers.
 To NASCAR fans, he's Dale Earnhardt Jr., a Hall of Famer and one of the sport's most beloved drivers .
 To Isla and Nicole, he's simply Dad.
 And apparently, the family chauffeur.
